description:
Sieniawa Palace began as a residence of the Sieniawski family in the second half of the 17th century — sources differ on the exact founding date — surrounded at the time with earthen fortifications. Italian artists later worked on the residence for Elżbieta and Adam Sieniawski, giving the estate an artistic standing befitting one of the leading families of the region.

The Czartoryski family acquired the property in 1731 and had it remodelled in the Classical style in 1763. After the fall of the November Uprising and the confiscation of the family's Puławy estate, Sieniawa became their main residence, and the palace entered its most significant period as a cultural and intellectual centre of south-eastern Poland, drawing artists such as Juliusz Kossak. Bolesław Podczaszyński carried out a further reconstruction in 1881–1883, adding Neo-Baroque features to the building.

The palace was ravaged during the First World War and rebuilt only in the second half of the 20th century. An 18th-century geometric garden survives at the front of the building, and the palace now operates as a hotel.
history: The palace at Sieniawa began as a residence of the Sieniawski family in the second half of the 17th century, surrounded with earthen fortifications, and Italian artists later worked on it for Elżbieta and Adam Sieniawski. The Czartoryski family acquired it in 1731 and remodelled it in the Classical style in 1763; after the fall of the November Uprising and the confiscation of their Puławy estate it became their main residence. Bolesław Podczaszyński reconstructed it in 1881–1883, adding Neo-Baroque features. During the Czartoryski period it was a cultural and intellectual centre of south-eastern Poland. The palace was ravaged in the First World War and rebuilt in the second half of the 20th century, and it now houses a hotel.

faqs.question: Who built Sieniawa Palace?
faqs.answer: It began as a residence of the Sieniawski family in the second half of the 17th century (sources differ on the exact date); the Czartoryski family acquired it in 1731 and remodelled it in 1763 and again in 1881–1883.

faqs.question: Is the palace original?
faqs.answer: It was ravaged in the First World War and rebuilt in the second half of the 20th century, so what you see is a reconstructed historic palace.

hotel.how_to_stay:
**Getting there:** In Sieniawa at Tadeusza Kościuszki 30, in the Subcarpathian Voivodeship.

**Rooms & rates:** From approx. €57/night for a Double Room with two twin beds or a King Room, both with a private bathroom, garden view and flat-screen TV; about €5 in taxes is shown separately on Booking. Breakfast is about €11 extra, and free cancellation was offered on the rate seen.

**On-site:** Rooms look onto the garden, and an 18th-century geometric garden is preserved at the front of the palace.

**Good to know:** The palace was ravaged in the First World War and rebuilt in the second half of the 20th century, so expect a historic building that has been substantially reconstructed. Breakfast is charged separately.

**Combine with:** [Krasiczyn Castle](/castles/poland/krasiczyn-castle) and [Dubiecko Castle](/castles/poland/dubiecko-castle), two other castle hotels in the Subcarpathian Voivodeship.
